description: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieve the first controlled, sustained and heavier-than-air human flight in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
A massive earthquake followed by devastating fires destroys a large portion of San Francisco, California.

historical_event_title: Roald Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
description: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and his team become the first humans to reach the geographic South Pole.
The British ocean liner RMS Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic Ocean after colliding with an iceberg during its maiden voyage.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in Sarajevo triggers the outbreak of World War I.
The Bolsheviks led by Vladimir Lenin overthrow the provisional government during the October Revolution, establishing Soviet rule.

historical_event_title: Signing of the Treaty of Versailles
description: The peace treaty officially ending World War I is signed at the Palace of Versailles, imposing heavy penalties on Germany.

historical_event_title: Establishment of the League of Nations
description: The international organization headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, is founded to promote global world peace.
British archaeologist Howard Carter discovers the virtually intact tomb of the 18th-dynasty Pharaoh Tutankhamun in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.
Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin, marking a monumental breakthrough in modern medicine and antibiotic treatments.
Stock prices collapse on the New York Stock Exchange, ushering in the global economic downturn known as the Great Depression.

historical_event_title: Inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt and the New Deal
description: FDR takes office amidst the Great Depression and introduces sweeping federal reform programs known as the New Deal.

historical_event_title: Opening of the Golden Gate Bridge
description: The iconic suspension bridge connecting San Francisco Bay to the Pacific Ocean officially opens to pedestrian and vehicular traffic.
Nazi Germany invades Poland, prompting the United Kingdom and France to declare war and initiating global conflict.
Imperial Japanese forces launch a surprise military strike on the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, drawing the US into WWII.

historical_event_title: End of World War II and Founding of the UN
description: World War II concludes with unconditional surrenders by Axis powers, leading directly to the establishment of the United Nations.
India achieves independence from British colonial rule after decades of non-violent resistance led by Mahatma Gandhi and others.
New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary and Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay successfully reach the summit of Mount Everest.

historical_event_title: Rosa Parks and the Montgomery Bus Boycott
description: Rosa Parks refuses to surrender her bus seat to a white passenger, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott and catalyzing the civil rights movement.
The Soviet Union successfully launches Sputnik 1, the world's first artificial satellite, kicking off the global Space Race.
A 13-day confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union over Soviet ballistic missiles deployed in Cuba brings the world to the brink of nuclear war.

historical_event_title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' Speech
description: During the March on Washington, civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his historic speech advocating for racial equality and civil rights.
American astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin land on the lunar surface, marking humanity's first footsteps on another celestial body.
Intel releases the world's first commercially available single-chip microprocessor, setting the foundation for the personal computing revolution.
US President Richard Nixon resigns from office following the Watergate political break-in scandal and impending impeachment proceedings.
NASA launches the Voyager 1 space probe to study the outer solar system and eventually interstellar space.
NASA successfully launches Columbia, the world's first reusable orbital spacecraft, on its maiden voyage.
Citizens breach the Berlin Wall, opening the border between East and West Berlin and marking the impending collapse of the Iron Curtain.

historical_event_title: Launch of the World Wide Web
description: Tim Berners-Lee launches the first-ever web server and browser to the general public, forever transforming global communication.
The Soviet Union officially ceases to exist as an independent nation, splitting into 15 separate post-Soviet republics and ending the Cold War.
Nelson Mandela wins South Africa's first fully representative democratic election, formally dismantling the apartheid regime.
IBM's supercomputer Deep Blue defeats reigning world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a historic six-game match.
Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launch Wikipedia, establishing the world's largest collaborative free online encyclopedia.
Mark Zuckerberg and fellow Harvard college roommates launch Facebook from their dormitory room, revolutionizing social networking.
Steve Jobs introduces the original iPhone at Macworld, transforming mobile telephony, computing, and digital culture.

historical_event_title: Global Financial Crisis and Bitcoin Whitepaper
description: A severe global economic downturn unfolds following the US subprime mortgage crisis, coinciding with the publication of the Bitcoin whitepaper.
CERN scientists working at the Large Hadron Collider announce the discovery of the Higgs Boson elementary particle.

historical_event_title: Adoption of the Paris Climate Agreement
description: Representatives from 196 nations adopt a legally binding international treaty on climate change addressing greenhouse gas emissions mitigation.
The World Health Organization officially declares the outbreak of the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) a global pandemic.

historical_event_title: Launch of the James Webb Space Telescope
description: NASA successfully launches the James Webb Space Telescope, designed to peer further back into the universe than any previous telescope.
